title: Dove Emoji 🕊️ Meaning: Peace, Loss and Rest in Peace
description: The 🕊️ dove emoji means peace, and very often condolences for someone who has died. Learn its religious, wedding and anti-war uses and how to send it kindly.
summary: The 🕊️ dove emoji is a white dove, usually carrying an olive branch, that stands for peace. In everyday messaging it is most often a gentle way to mark a death, equivalent to “rest in peace.” Christians also use it for the Holy Spirit, and it appears at weddings and in calls to end wars.
meaning: The dove with an olive branch comes from the story of Noah, where the bird returns to the ark with a leaf as proof the flood is ending. From there it became the universal emblem of peace, reinforced in the twentieth century by Picasso’s dove drawings for the peace movement. The emoji carries that meaning directly: ceasefire news, anti-war protests, international days of peace and calls for calm all use it.

On social media, though, you will meet 🕊️ most often after a death. It has become the standard emoji of condolence, softer than a coffin and less religious than praying hands. People add it to “rest easy,” to the name of someone they have lost and to anniversary posts. When a celebrity dies, tributes fill with doves. If someone’s username or bio includes a name followed by this emoji, they are almost certainly honoring a person who has passed.

Christian usage is its own strand. In the Gospels the Holy Spirit descends like a dove at Jesus’ baptism, so the bird marks baptisms, confirmations, Pentecost and expressions of faith. White doves are released at some weddings as a sign of love and fidelity, and the emoji appears on invitations for that reason. Away from ceremony, it expresses personal calm: making peace with a situation, protecting your peace, letting something go.

contexts.label: In condolences
contexts.body: Sent after a loss, the dove says “I’m sorry” and “may they rest in peace” without many words. It is appropriate across most cultures and beliefs because it reads as peaceful rather than doctrinal. It pairs naturally with 🤍 or 🙏. Use it on its own line or after the person’s name.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Outside mourning, it settles arguments. “Truce? 🕊️” offers an olive branch after a fight. People also use it to describe freeing themselves from stress, as in “blocked him, at peace 🕊️.” It has a calm, grown-up tone and is rarely used as a joke.

contexts.label: In religion
contexts.body: Churches and believers use it in posts about baptism, confirmation and Pentecost, and beside Bible verses about the Spirit or peace. It appears in Easter and Christmas greetings as well. In this setting it is a statement of faith, often accompanied by ✝️ or 🙏.

contexts.label: Around the world
contexts.body: During wars and crises the dove spreads widely in posts calling for ceasefires and expressing solidarity with civilians. It is used by people on different sides of a conflict and by those taking none, which makes it one of the few symbols that stays mostly non-partisan.

confusedWith.difference: 🐦 is a generic small bird, typically blue, for nature, birdsong and chirpy moods. It has no symbolic weight. Using it in a condolence message would look like a mistake, while 🕊️ is immediately understood.

☮️ is the circular sign from the nuclear disarmament movement, tied to activism, the 1960s and hippie culture. The dove expresses the same ideal more softly and is the only one of the two used for mourning.
🙏 means prayer, thanks or pleading. It is common in condolences too, but it focuses on the sender’s act of praying. The dove focuses on the person at rest. Many messages include both.

avoid: Avoid using it flippantly, for example to joke that your phone has “died,” around people who are grieving.
Do not send only a dove to a close friend who has lost someone; add words so it does not feel like a minimal response.
Skip it when you are not ready to make peace, because it signals that the conflict is over.
design: Most vendors show a white dove in flight, in profile, with a green olive sprig in its beak. Apple, Google and Samsung all include the branch, which anchors the peace meaning. Wing position and outline color vary slightly, and a few designs omit or shrink the sprig. On some older systems the emoji may appear as a plain black-and-white symbol instead of a colored picture.

faqs.q: What does 🕊️ mean after someone’s name?
faqs.a: It almost always means that person has died and is being remembered. Friends and relatives add the dove to names in bios, captions and comments as a quiet form of “rest in peace.”

faqs.q: What does 🕊️ mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: They may be offering peace after a disagreement, sharing that they feel calm, or expressing sympathy. It is a sincere emoji with no flirtatious meaning. If you recently argued, take it as a white flag.

It can be. In Christianity the dove represents the Holy Spirit and appears at baptisms and Pentecost. But the peace and mourning meanings are understood by people of any faith or none, so it is not exclusively religious.

faqs.q: Can I use 🕊️ to say sorry for your loss?
faqs.a: Yes. It is among the most widely accepted condolence emojis. Pair it with a short written message, such as the person’s name or a memory, so your sympathy feels personal and not automatic.

faqs.q: What does 🕊️ mean on Instagram or TikTok?
faqs.a: Typically remembrance in tribute posts, or the “protecting my peace” attitude in lifestyle content. During international conflicts it is used in calls for peace. The meaning does not differ between the two apps.
